title: The Watershed Where All Refusals Eventually Gather

features.name: confluence of refusals
features.desc-on-touch: Here the stream gathers what the town turned away—scraps, decisions unmade, letters never sent. The water doesn't judge; it carries, and something in this gathering teaches the discarded things they were always meant to meet here.

features.name: sediment archive
features.desc-on-touch: The bed speaks in layers: what was discarded first lies deepest, overlaid by all the refusals that followed, pressed into meaning by the weight of water and time.

features.name: weir of reconsidered things
features.desc-on-touch: A barrier built from what was deemed worthless, now holding back the flow, now letting it through. Something reconsiders itself here, slowly.

features.name: bank where things learn their names
features.desc-on-touch: The exposed earth holds objects half-buried. Each one waits for the water to finish its sentence—to speak aloud what the refusal tried to silence.

features.name: mirror in motion
features.desc-on-touch: The water's surface breaks and reforms constantly, holding the sky, holding the banks, holding everything that was refused a place, giving them all a place to see themselves reflected.

features.name: clearing that grew from spillage
features.desc-on-touch: The overflow carved this space and left it green. What was refused nourished the place the refusal could not reach.

inscription: all the town's no-longer-wanted things teach the water how to say yes

reverie.title: REVERIE — the creek in afternoon
narr: You wade where the water has gathered what the
town refused. She stands on the bank, pointing at
something caught in the current. The refusal was
never about the thing itself, she says. The water
teaches it a different name. You both listen to the
creek speak it aloud, over and over, until it sounds true.

exits.label: northward back toward the roots and hidden water
following the current toward wider country
